def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data:
## Definition

Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and the unit cell $Y=(0,1)^d$ with Lebesgue measure $|Y|=1$. Assume Countable Choice for the $L^2$ conventions of [[def-countable-choice]]. A **uniformly elliptic periodic scalar diffusion coefficient** is a measurable real function $a:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ such that $a(y+k)=a(y)$ for almost every $y$ and every $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and there are constants $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$ with $\lambda\le a(y)\le\Lambda$ almost everywhere on $Y$. Coefficients are identified when they agree almost everywhere.

For $\epsilon>0$, the physical scalar coefficient is $a_\epsilon(x)=a(x/\epsilon)$ and the associated matrix is $a_\epsilon(x)I_d$. The bounded-domain branch used on this page is $\Omega=(0,1)^d$ with homogeneous zero boundary values. Its weak equation for datum $f\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is
$$\int_\Omega a(x/\epsilon)\nabla u_\epsilon\cdot\nabla v\,dx=\int_\Omega fv\,dx\qquad(v\in H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)).$$
No coefficient regularity beyond measurability and the displayed bounds is part of this definition.
def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space:
## Definition

Fix $d\ge1$, $Y=(0,1)^d$, and Countable Choice for the Sobolev conventions of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $C^\infty_\#(Y)$ be the restrictions to $Y$ of smooth $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic real functions on $\mathbb R^d$. Define
$$H^1_\#(Y):=\overline{C^\infty_\#(Y)}^{\,H^1(Y)},\qquad V_\#:=\left\{v\in H^1_\#(Y):\int_Yv\,dy=0\right\}.$$
The integral is the normalized cell mean because $|Y|=1$. Derivatives are weak derivatives on $Y$ and the periodic condition is the closure convention in this definition; no pointwise boundary trace is being imposed. Equip $V_\#$ with the inherited $H^1$ norm.
def-periodic-cell-problem:
## Definition

For coefficient $a$, cell $Y$, and zero-mean periodic space $V_\#$ from [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]] and [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]], and for $p\in\mathbb R^d$, the **weak periodic cell equation** asks for $\chi_p\in V_\#$ such that
$$\int_Y a(y)(p+\nabla_y\chi_p(y))\cdot\nabla_yv(y)\,dy=0\qquad(v\in V_\#).$$
The sign convention is $p+\nabla_y\chi_p$; the zero-mean condition fixes the additive constant. This definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.
lem-periodic-cell-poincare:
## Statement

Let $Y=(0,1)^d$ and $V_\#$ be the mean-zero periodic $H^1$ space of [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]]. Then every $v\in V_\#$ satisfies
$$\|v\|_{L^2(Y)}\le\sqrt d\,\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(Y)},$$
and every $v\in H^1_\#(Y)$ satisfies $\int_Y\nabla v=0$. Consequently $\|\nabla v\|_2$ is a complete norm on $V_\#$ equivalent to its inherited $H^1$ norm.
lem-periodic-cell-corrector-wellposednes:
## Statement

Assume $a,\lambda,\Lambda,Y,V_\#$ are as in [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]] and [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]]. For each $p\in\mathbb R^d$, the equation in [[def-periodic-cell-problem]] has a unique solution $\chi_p\in V_\#$. The map $p\mapsto\chi_p$ is linear, and
$$\|\nabla\chi_p\|_{L^2(Y)}\le(\Lambda/\lambda)|p|,\qquad \|\chi_p\|_{L^2(Y)}\le\sqrt d(\Lambda/\lambda)|p|.$$
def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effecti:
## Definition

Let $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ be the standard basis of $\mathbb R^d$. By [[lem-periodic-cell-corrector-wellposedness]], let $\chi_j:=\chi_{e_j}$ be the unique mean-zero solution of the periodic cell equation. For $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)$ define $\chi_p=\sum_jp_j\chi_j$ and define the constant matrix $A^*$ by its columns:
$$A^*e_j:=\int_Ya(y)(e_j+\nabla\chi_j(y))\,dy.$$
Equivalently, $A^*p=\int_Ya(y)(p+\nabla\chi_p(y))dy$. All integrals are finite because $a\in L^\infty(Y)$ and $\nabla\chi_j\in L^2(Y)$. This definition does not itself assert symmetry or ellipticity.
thm-periodic-effective-tensor-symmetric-:
## Statement

Under the scalar periodic ellipticity hypotheses of [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]], the matrix $A^*$ of [[def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effective-tensor]] is symmetric and satisfies
$$\lambda |p|^2\le p\cdot A^*p\le\Lambda|p|^2\qquad(p\in\mathbb R^d).$$
lem-periodic-averaging-on-cube:
## Statement

Let $Y=(0,1)^d$, $Q=(0,1)^d$, $g\in L^1(Y)$ be extended $\mathbb Z^d$-periodically, and $\varphi\in C_c^1(Q)$. As $\epsilon\downarrow0$,
$$\int_Q\varphi(x)g(x/\epsilon)\,dx\longrightarrow\left(\int_Yg\right)\left(\int_Q\varphi\right).$$
If $g\in L^2(Y)$ and $0<\epsilon\le1$, then $\|g(\cdot/\epsilon)\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C_d\|g\|_{L^2(Y)}$. In particular, for $g\in L^2(Y)$, $g(\cdot/\epsilon)\rightharpoonup\int_Yg$ weakly in $L^2(Q)$.
def-periodic-two-scale-convergence:
## Definition

Let $Q=Y=(0,1)^d$, let $\epsilon_n>0$ tend to zero, and let $(u_n)$ be bounded in $L^2(Q)$. We say $u_n$ **two-scale converges weakly** to $u\in L^2(Q\times Y)$ along $(\epsilon_n)$ if for every finite sum
$$\Phi(x,y)=\sum_{r=1}^m\phi_r(x)\psi_r(y),\quad \phi_r\in C_c^\infty(Q),\quad\psi_r\in C_\#^\infty(Y),$$
one has
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_Qu_n(x)\Phi(x,x/\epsilon_n)\,dx=\int_Q\int_Yu(x,y)\Phi(x,y)\,dy\,dx.$$
Here $C_\#^\infty(Y)$ is the smooth $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic class from [[def-periodic-zero-mean-cell-space]]. The test definition is independent of how a finite sum is represented because both sides are linear in $\Phi$.
thm-two-scale-compactness-for-l2-bounded:
## Statement

Let $Q=Y=(0,1)^d$, let $\epsilon_n\downarrow0$ (monotonicity may be dropped; only $\epsilon_n\to0$ is used), and suppose $(u_n)$ is bounded in $L^2(Q)$. Then some subsequence two-scale converges in the sense of [[def-periodic-two-scale-convergence]] to a function $u\in L^2(Q\times Y)$.
lem-unit-cube-h01-separability-and-l2-co:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and let $Q=(0,1)^d$, $d\ge1$. Then $H^1_0(Q;\mathbb R)$ is a separable real Hilbert space. It satisfies
$$\|v\|_{L^2(Q)}\le\|\partial_1v\|_{L^2(Q)}\le\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(Q)}\qquad(v\in H^1_0(Q)).$$
Moreover, every sequence bounded in $H^1_0(Q)$ has a subsequence converging in $L^2(Q)$. These conclusions use Countable Choice only; no Axiom of Choice or Dependent Choice is needed in the proof below.
lem-two-scale-gradient-decomposition-for:
## Statement

Let $Q=Y=(0,1)^d$, $\epsilon_n\to0$, and $(u_n)$ be bounded in $H^1_0(Q)$. There are a subsequence, $u\in H^1_0(Q)$, and $u_1\in L^2(Q;V_\#)$ such that $u_n\rightharpoonup u$ in $H^1_0(Q)$, $u_n\to u$ in $L^2(Q)$, and
$$\nabla u_n\overset{2}{\rightharpoonup}\nabla_xu(x)+\nabla_yu_1(x,y).$$
thm-periodic-dirichlet-homogenization-on:
## Statement

Let $Q=(0,1)^d$, let $a$ be a measurable $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic scalar coefficient with $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$, and let $f\in L^2(Q)$. For $\epsilon>0$ let $u_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ be the unique weak solution
$$\int_Qa(x/\epsilon)\nabla u_\epsilon\cdot\nabla v=\int_Qfv\qquad(v\in H^1_0(Q)).$$
Let $u_0\in H^1_0(Q)$ be the unique solution with $A^*$ from [[def-periodic-cell-correctors-and-effective-tensor]] in place of $a(x/\epsilon)I$. Then as $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $u_\epsilon\rightharpoonup u_0$ in $H^1_0(Q)$.
cor-periodic-dirichlet-homogenization-st:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-periodic-dirichlet-homogenization-on-unit-cube]], $u_\epsilon\to u_0$ strongly in $L^2(Q)$.
lem-periodic-flux-corrector:
## Statement

For each column $j$, define the mean-zero periodic flux $q^j(y)=a(y)(e_j+\nabla\chi_j(y))-A^*e_j$. There is a mean-zero periodic tensor $\sigma^j\in H^1_\#(Y;\mathbb R^{d\times d})$ such that $\sigma^j_{ik}=-\sigma^j_{ki}$ and
$$q_i^j=\sum_{k=1}^d\partial_{y_k}\sigma^j_{ik}\quad\text{in distributions on the torus},\qquad \|\sigma^j\|_{H^1(Y)}\le C_d\|q^j\|_{L^2(Y)}.$$
thm-periodic-boundary-layer-corrector-es:
## Statement

Let $Q=(0,1)^d$, $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$ be scalar and periodic, and let $f\in L^2(Q)$. For each $\epsilon>0$, let $u_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ solve the oscillatory weak equation with coefficient $a(x/\epsilon)$, and suppose $u_0\in C^2(\overline Q)\cap H^1_0(Q)$ solves the homogenized equation with the same datum $f$. For $0<\epsilon\le1/4$ choose a Lipschitz cutoff $\eta_\epsilon$ equal to zero where $\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial Q)\le\epsilon$, equal to one where that distance is at least $2\epsilon$, and with $|\nabla\eta_\epsilon|\le C_d/\epsilon$. Define
$$w_\epsilon(x)=u_0(x)+\epsilon\eta_\epsilon(x)\sum_{j=1}^d\chi_j(x/\epsilon)\partial_ju_0(x).$$
Then $w_\epsilon\in H^1_0(Q)$ and, for a constant independent of $\epsilon$,
$$\|\nabla(u_\epsilon-w_\epsilon)\|_{L^2(Q)}+\|u_\epsilon-u_0\|_{L^2(Q)}\le C\sqrt\epsilon.$$
The constant may depend on $d,\lambda,\Lambda$, the fixed corrector and flux-potential $H^1(Y)$ norms, $\|u_0\|_{C^2(\overline Q)}$, and the cutoff profile. No rate is asserted without this regularity and periodicity.
alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro:
## Definition

This is a real-arithmetic finite-dimensional FE-HMM discretization; no bit-complexity or coefficient-oracle claim is made. Fix $Q=(0,1)^2$ and coefficient $a$ from [[def-periodic-scalar-diffusion-data]]. Use the diagonal of the square from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$ as a two-triangle initial matching macro mesh. Label that shared diagonal $0$ in both triangles and each exterior edge $1$. It is a compatible labeled mesh in the sense of [[def-afem-nvb-labelled-triangulation-family]]. The macro input is any finite admissible descendant triangulation $\mathcal T$ of this mesh. Its cells are closed affine triangles as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]].

Choose $\epsilon>0$, a micro side length $\delta>0$, $f\in L^2(Q)$, and a finite matching triangulation $\mathcal M$ of the unit square whose opposite boundary edges and vertices match under translation by $e_1,e_2$. The periodic micro space is
$$W_{\mathcal M}:=\{z\in V_\#:z\text{ is continuous and affine on every triangle of }\mathcal M\}.$$
It is a finite-dimensional subspace of $V_\#$; the periodic closure condition identifies opposite traces. Let $V_H$ be the conforming zero-boundary continuous piecewise-affine macro space on $\mathcal T$, using [[def-broken-and-conforming-polynomial-spaces]]. Its inclusion in $H^1_0(Q)$ is supplied by [[thm-matching-continuous-piecewise-polynomials-are-wkp]] and [[thm-zero-boundary-piecewise-polynomials-in-w10p]].

For each macro triangle $K$, use its barycenter $x_K$ as the single quadrature point with positive weight $|K|$. Set $b_K(y)=a(x_K/\epsilon+(\delta/\epsilon)y)$ on $Y$. For each coordinate vector $e_j$, solve the finite periodic micro problem
$$w^h_{K,j}\in W_{\mathcal M},\qquad \int_Y b_K(y)(e_j+\nabla_yw^h_{K,j})\cdot\nabla_yz_h\,dy=0\quad(z_h\in W_{\mathcal M}),$$
and set $A^h_Ke_j=\int_Yb_K(y)(e_j+\nabla_yw^h_{K,j})dy$. Assemble
$$B_H(U,V)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}|K|\,\nabla U|_K\cdot A^h_K\nabla V|_K.$$
The macro output $U_H\in V_H$ solves $B_H(U_H,V)=\int_QfV$ for every $V\in V_H$. If $V_H=\{0\}$ this means $U_H=0$. Otherwise it is a finite linear system in the interior macro vertex values. [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]] proves every micro and macro system is nonsingular. The centroid quadrature is positive and exact for constants, which is the only quadrature property used in the error theorem.
lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposednes:
## Statement

For every macro cell $K$ in [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]], the coefficient $b_K$ satisfies $\lambda\le b_K\le\Lambda$. For each $p\in\mathbb R^2$, both the full cell problem on $V_\#$ and its restriction to $W_{\mathcal M}$ have unique solutions $w_{K,p}$ and $w^h_{K,p}$. The tensors
$$A_K^{\rm ex}p=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w_{K,p}),\qquad A_K^hp=\int_Yb_K(p+\nabla w^h_{K,p})$$
are symmetric and satisfy $\lambda I\le A_K^{\rm ex},A_K^h\le\Lambda I$. Consequently the macro FE-HMM system in the algorithm has a unique solution.
lem-fehmm-micro-tensor-approximation-err:
## Statement

For a fixed macro sample $K$ in [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]], let $b_K$ be its sampled coefficient, $w_{K,p}\in V_\#$ the full periodic cell solution, and $w^h_{K,p}\in W_{\mathcal M}$ its micro P1 solution from [[lem-fehmm-micro-cell-solves-wellposedness]]. Set $\|\nabla v\|_{b_K}^2=\int_Yb_K|\nabla v|^2$. Then
$$p\cdot(A_K^h-A_K^{\rm ex})p=\|\nabla(w^h_{K,p}-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}^2\ge0,$$
and for any $z_h\in W_{\mathcal M}$,
$$\|\nabla(w^h_{K,p}-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}\le\|\nabla(z_h-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}.$$
In particular $\|A_K^h-A_K^{\rm ex}\|_{op}\le\eta_K^2$, where $\eta_K=\sup_{|p|=1}\inf_{z_h\in W_{\mathcal M}}\|\nabla(z_h-w_{K,p})\|_{b_K}$ and $\|M\|_{op}=\sup_{|p|=1}|Mp|$.
lem-fehmm-period-aligned-sampling-has-ze:
## Statement

For any dimension $d$, phase $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$, and positive integer $m$, let $b(y)=a(\theta+my)$ on $Y$. Let $w_p\in V_\#$ be the unique mean-zero minimizer of $\int_Yb(y)|p+\nabla v(y)|^2dy$ and define $A_{\theta,m}^{\rm ex}p=\int_Yb(y)(p+\nabla w_p(y))dy$. Then $A_{\theta,m}^{\rm ex}=A^*$ for every $p\in\mathbb R^d$. Thus a micro side length $\delta=m\epsilon$ has zero continuum sampling/resonance error, regardless of phase; a separate finite micro-space error can remain.
lem-fehmm-one-dimensional-nonaligned-res:
## Statement

In one dimension, let $a$ be measurable, $1$-periodic, and satisfy $0<\lambda\le a\le\Lambda$. For a phase $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and ratio $r=\delta/\epsilon\ge1$, let $w_r\in V_\#$ solve $\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')v'\,dy=0$ for every $v\in V_\#$, and define $A_r(\theta)=\int_0^1a(\theta+ry)(1+w_r')\,dy$. Then
$$A_r(\theta)=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(\theta+ry)}\right)^{-1},\qquad A^*=\left(\int_0^1\frac{dy}{a(y)}\right)^{-1},$$
and
$$|A_r(\theta)-A^*|\le\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda r}=\frac{2\Lambda^2}{\lambda}\frac\epsilon\delta.$$
No dimension-independent bound for the unaligned case is claimed here.
thm-fehmm-macro-micro-resonance-error-de:
## Statement

Let $U_H$ be the FE-HMM solution from [[alg-fehmm-periodic-cell-micro-macro]] on a matching macro triangulation of $Q=(0,1)^2$, and let $u_0\in H^1_0(Q)$ solve the homogenized equation with coefficient $A^*$. For each macro cell let $A_K^{\rm ex}$ be the exact periodic-coupling sampled tensor and $A_K^h$ its discrete micro tensor. Define
$$\Delta_{\rm micro}=\max_K\|A_K^h-A_K^{\rm ex}\|_{op},\qquad \Delta_{\rm res}=\max_K\|A_K^{\rm ex}-A^*\|_{op},\qquad \Delta=\Delta_{\rm micro}+\Delta_{\rm res},$$
and $\eta_H=\inf_{V\in V_H}\|\nabla(u_0-V)\|_{L^2(Q)}$. If $\Delta<\lambda$, then
$$\|\nabla(U_H-u_0)\|_2\le\frac{\lambda+\Lambda}{\lambda-\Delta}\,\eta_H+\frac{\Delta}{\lambda-\Delta}\,\|\nabla u_0\|_2.$$
The first term is macro best approximation; the second is explicitly split by $\Delta_{\rm micro}$ and $\Delta_{\rm res}$. By [[lem-fehmm-micro-tensor-approximation-error]], $\Delta_{\rm micro}\le\max_K\eta_K^2$. If every micro ratio is an integer, [[lem-fehmm-period-aligned-sampling-has-zero-resonance]] gives $\Delta_{\rm res}=0$. The condition $\Delta<\lambda$ is a sufficient perturbation condition; no arbitrary-scale accuracy is asserted.
